systems: systemd-fstab-generator turns an x-systemd.automount fstab line into an .automount and .mount unit; the unit holds the options from the last daemon-reload, not the current fstab, so the reload must come before anything re-triggers the path
autofs: any access to the trigger point (ls, stat, mount.cifs resolving the mountpoint) makes systemd mount the unit, which is how a forjar mount -t ended up stacked over systemd's
util-linux findmnt lists every filesystem mounted at a target, bottom first, so tail -1 reads the top mount only; umount(8) -l detaches a busy mount lazily, which is why the automount path refuses it
crux.verdict: CHANGELOG-worthy behaviour change for x-systemd.automount mounts: a stack is RED and apply lets systemd mount from a reloaded unit. Plain mounts are unchanged. #647 is test-only.
